did: Built and tested this round, in two halves. Bulk texts: the owner opened Bulk texts, chose pharmacies as the audience, saw at once how many people would get it (5, 2 texts each, 10 in all, against a daily limit of 2,000), wrote an Eid offer and sent it. Affiliates: the owner made a promoter called Rima with a 3 percent share and the link /a/RIMA3; an order placed through the link was counted and a payout was written down.

checks.text: Bulk texts: the audience can be narrowed by type (public, pharmacy, wholesale), tier, area, days since the last order and whether they owe us; before sending, the screen says how many will get it, how many texts each, how many in all and how many of today's limit are used
Every text ends with a line to stop the messages (a link that works without signing in); anyone who stops is left out next time, and a person who opted out never gets another campaign text

The campaign page lists each person (number hidden except the last digits) with sent, failed or waiting; it can be stopped, and started again where it stopped; the sending speed and the daily limit are settings

Affiliates: the promoter's page shows the link, visits, orders and what has been earned and paid; the share applies to finished orders only and comes back off on a return or cancellation; the link leaves a code on the visitor's phone for the number of days set in Settings, and a buyer is never their own promoter's customer
A payout pays what is owed in full, is written down with how it was paid (cash, bKash, Nagad, Rocket or bank) and a note, and is refused when nothing is owed (23 and 21 automatic tests)

notes: Built this round. The texts go out through whichever SMS service the owner connected in Connections (the same one used for order messages); in this test they went through the test gateway, so NOT verified: delivery to a real phone and the real gateway's own limits. Money to promoters is paid by the owner outside the site and written down here; nothing is sent to any payment service.
